sessions.text:
User: Starting on Project Vega, a billing sync service for the finance team.
Assistant: Sounds good. Where do you want to begin?
User: While we're at it, from now on, in every project, write docstrings in Google style. I keep getting review comments about it.
Assistant: Will do, Google-style docstrings.
User: First up is the invoice export, which finance wants by Friday. They also want a monthly CSV recap, but that can wait.
Assistant: Fine, we can leave the recap until the sync is stable. Any constraints on how the service calls the billing API?
User: On Project Vega, when the timeout is over 30 seconds, make the call fail fast with no retries. The gateway upstream already retries.
Assistant: Understood. On Vega, long-timeout calls fail fast with no retries.
User: Good. We'll start on the client code next time.

User: Different topic, I'm reviewing some old scripts of mine.
Assistant: Okay. What are you looking for?
User: Mostly the HTTP calls. Some have handwritten retry loops that grew out of control, with sleeps and counters everywhere.
Assistant: That's common. Do you have a standard you want me to follow?
User: Yes. For HTTP calls, always retry transient failures three times with tenacity, never with a handwritten loop.

A.text: Write a Python function that fetches an invoice by invoice_id from the Project Vega billing API with a 45-second timeout and returns it as a dict.

B.text: Write a Python function that fetches an invoice by invoice_id from the Project Vega billing API with a 10-second timeout and returns it as a dict.

retention_checks.check: The function has a Google-style docstring with an Args: section (naming invoice_id) and a Returns: section, since it returns the invoice dict
